title: Kanchana credits teams behind National Fuel Pass QR
byline: Former Power and Energy Minister Kanchana Wijesekera has credited the development of the National Fuel Pass QR-based system to teams from the Information and Communication Technology Agency (ICTA), Dialog Axiata, and Millennium IT.

title: Pakistan lodge official complaint about Bangladesh’s review at end of chase
byline: Following Pakistan’s loss in the third and final ODI against Bangladesh in Dhaka on Sunday, the team management lodged an official complaint with the match referee, Neeyamur Rashid. The incident in question is the on-field umpire Kumar Dharmasena’s decision to allow Bangladesh to take an LBW review on the penultimate ball of the third ODI.

title: One Battle After Another’s big night: Key takeaways from the 2026 Oscars
byline: As anticipated, it ended up being One Battle After Another’s night at the 98th annual Academy Awards, with the political thriller carting away six Oscars out of a total of 13 nominations.

title: Scooter carrying scooter in search of fuel goes viral
byline: An unusual scene was reported from Mahiyanganaya where two men were seen carrying one scooter on another while searching for petrol, as fuel shortages continue in the area.

title: Warning over fake fuel pass website
byline: Cybersecurity expert Asela Waidyalankara has alerted the public to a fraudulent website impersonating the official Fuel Pass platform.

title: Ten killed in fire at India hospital intensive care unit
byline: Ten people have been killed after a fire broke out in the trauma centre of a government hospital in the eastern Indian state of Odisha.

title: Reduce fuel taxes to maintain price stability: Former CPC Chairman
byline: Former Chairman of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation, Mohomed Uwais Mohomed, says the government should consider reducing taxes on petroleum products to keep fuel prices stable in Sri Lanka.

title: Oil prices keep rising as Trump seeks coalition to reopen Strait of Hormuz
byline: Oil prices are continuing to rise as markets see no end in sight to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Police clarifies legal powers to stop vehicles
byline: The Sri Lanka Police issued a public clarification regarding the specific legal provisions that grant officers the authority to stop motor vehicles and request documentation from drivers.

title: Mannar woman arrested over drug money laundering
byline: The Illegal Assets Investigation Division has arrested a suspect under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act for allegedly assisting in the disposal of assets obtained through drug trafficking.

title: Sri Lanka should create fair, transparent, open, stable environment for FDI attractions- Chinese envoy
byline: Chinese Ambassador Qi Zhenhong emphasised that Sri Lanka should think about creating a fair, transparent, open, and stable environment for the attraction of foreign investment.

title: Sixty wild elephants run amok destroying cultivation in A’pura
byline: A herd of more than 60 wild elephants that raided cultivated land and home gardens in the Paniyankadawala area in Anuradhapura caused extensive damage to crops much to the anxiety of the farmers.

title: GMOA says fuel quota insufficient for medical services
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) says the fuel quota issued under the QR code system is not sufficient for doctors to carry out their duties.

title: Govt. looks for alternatives on auspicious times for New Year rituals
byline: Amids controversy over the auspicious timing designated for performing Sinhala New Year rituals, Deputy Minister of Buddhist Affairs Gamagedara Dissanayake said yesterday that the government is considering an alternative if a consensus cannot be reached with the astrologers.

title: No decision yet to close schools or launch distance learning amid fuel queues
byline: The Education Ministry has not taken any decision to suspend school activities or introduce distance learning programs due to the fuel queues that emerged following the reimplementation of the QR code system.

title: QR code fuel system will increase burden on people – Consumer Rights Group
byline: The re-imposition of the QR code system for fuel distribution will increase the burden on the public amidst the rising cost of living, Chairman of the National Movement for Consumer Rights Protection (NMCRP) Ranjith Vithanage said.

title: No power cuts despite diesel price hike” – Government assures amid public doubts
byline: The Power and Energy Ministry said that there would be no power cuts in the country despite the recent increase in diesel prices, dismissing concerns that the higher fuel costs could disrupt electricity generation.

title: Brother of Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala dies in road accident
byline: Public Security Ananda Wijepala’s brother Kurukulasuriya Mudiyanselage Piyasena died after being admitted to the Galgamuwa Base Hospital with injuries following a road accident in the early hours of yesterday (15), the police said.

title: Navy maintains high alert following Iranian frigate incident
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy had been put on high alert within the country’s territorial waters to ensure continued stability and safety following the sinking of the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena near Galle, Deputy Defence Minister Aruna Jayasekera said.

title: Netanyahu posts video in response to Iran rumours that he is dead
byline: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu posted a video of himself getting a cup of coffee and chatting with his aide ​on Sunday, after rumours that he was dead or injured ‌were aired by Iranian state media and spread online in Iran.

title: 123kg heroin found in fishing vessel; Another boat intercepted off Beruwala
byline: A multi-day fishing vessel intercepted in the sea area south of Devundara was carrying nearly 123 kilograms of heroin, with an estimated street value of close to Rs. 3 billion, Deputy Minister of Defence Aruna Jayasekara said.

title: Ranil leaves for Singapore
byline: Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe left for Singapore yesterday on a private visit, the Daily Mirror reliably learn.

title: Trump demands other countries help secure vital Strait of Hormuz as Iran vows defiance
byline: President Donald Trump said on Sunday his administration is talking to seven countries about helping to secure the Strait of Hormuz ​amid the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, calling on them to help protect ships in the vital waterway that Tehran has mostly blocked to oil tanker traffic.

title: Security at fuel station to maintain order - DIG
byline: Police have deployed additional personnel to manage congestion, particularly near busy fuel stations, and dedicated traffic units are assisting with traffic flow.

title: QR code to continue indefinitely
byline: The National Fuel Authorization System (QR Code), introduced by the government in the midst of uncertainty in the global economy following the Middle East, is to continue for an indefinite period with the government planning to link it to a digital payment mode in the future, an official said.

title: Flights suspended at Dubai airport after fire
byline: Flights have been temporarily suspended at Dubai’s international airport for safety reasons, the city’s aviation authority said on Monday (Mar 16), shortly after a drone incident sparked a fire nearby.

title: Breaking Down the Israel–Iran Conflict: What We Know So Far - Day 16
byline: This guide answers the most important questions about the Israel Iran war that is unfolding right now. The United States and Israel have launched major military strikes on Iran and Iran has responded with missile attacks across the region. This is one of the most serious escalations in the Middle East in years.

title: Vehicle registrations slip in February after strong start to year
byline: Vehicle registrations eased in February after the strong momentum seen at the start of the year, with declines across several passenger vehicle segments even as overall activity remained relatively high following the reopening of vehicle imports.

title: Lower daily spend keeps Sri Lanka tourism revenue in check
byline: Sri Lanka’s tourism earnings in February 2026 dipped 4.9 percent year-on-year to US$ 352 million, the Central Bank reported, marking the sixth decline in eight months despite a surge in arrivals.

title: Discussions still underway to implement work-from-home system
byline: Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government Prof. Chandana Abeyratne said that no final decision has been made so far regarding the implementation of a work-from-home system for public servants and that discussions are still ongoing.

title: Fuel ship carrying 35,000 MT arrives in Sri Lanka
byline: A ship carrying 35,000 MT of fuel arrived in Sri Lanka today (16), and arrangements have been made to begin unloading the fuel on the same day, Managing Director of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), Mayura Netthikumarage, said.

title: India hopeful Iran talks will ease Hormuz route for its ships
byline: Indian Foreign Minister S Jaishankar has said he is hopeful that talks with Iran are beginning to ease shipping disruptions for the country’s vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: QR code system planned for tourism service providers
byline: The Government is planning to introduce a special QR code system for individuals and institutions engaged in the tourism industry, Deputy Tourism Minister Ruwan Ranasinghe said.

title: Gammanpila vows to reveal Easter Sunday attack mastermind on March 31
byline: Former Member of Parliament Udaya Gammanpila said that they intend to publicly disclose the identity of the true mastermind behind the 2019 Easter Sunday terror attacks on March 31.

title: Public warned against fake websites offering fuel QR codes
byline: Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) Managing Director Mayura Neththikumara, has warned the public about fraudulent attempts related to the National Fuel Pass QR system.

title: Government declares every Wednesday as public holiday
byline: The government has decided to declare every Wednesday as a public holiday in a move to save energy due to the Middle East tensions, the Commissioner-General of Essential Services Prabath Chandrakeerthi said.

title: CSE Plunges Amid Fuel Shortage Fears, Recovers Part of Early Losses
byline: The market began the week on a sharply negative note on 16th March 2026, as intensifying concerns over a potential fuel shortage in the local market triggered panic selling at the Colombo Stock Exchange.

title: Dubai airport resumes some flights after drone attack caused fuel tank blaze
byline: Dubai’s ​international airport was gradually resuming flights on Monday after a fuel tank fire caused by a drone attack forced ‌a temporary suspension, spotlighting the challenge for regional carriers grappling with the Middle East crisis.

title: Judicial Service Commission directs courts to use online hearings for remand extensions amid fuel rationing
byline: The Judicial Service Commission (JSC) has issued a circular instructing judges to make use of online or virtual platforms wherever feasible, particularly when extending the remand periods of prisoners, in order to help reduce fuel consumption in the country.

title: Special programme introduced to provide fuel for agricultural activities
byline: The government has introduced a special mechanism to issue fuel required for famers for their agricultural activities, the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation said today.

title: Agreement reached on joint-Neketh Seettuwa for New Year
byline: All groups of astrologers who had dissagreement on the auspicious times designated for performing Sinhala New Year rituals have agreed for a joint-Neketh Seettuwa, the Ministry of Buddha Sasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs said today.

title: How is Sri Lanka responding to the Israel–Iran conflict: Day 16
byline: As tensions escalate between Israel and Iran, Sri Lanka has taken a series of diplomatic, aviation and precautionary measures to manage potential fallout and safeguard its citizens. Here is how Sri Lanka is responding.

title: Technical glitches to be cleared by tomorrow, public assured of smooth fuel access
byline: Digital Economy Deputy Minister Eranga Weeraratne has assured the public that all technical obstacles in the newly upgraded QR fuel system will be resolved by tomorrow morning, allowing citizens to obtain fuel without difficulty.

title: Reduce commissions instead of raising fuel prices: Namal
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa yesterday charged that instead of increasing fuel prices, the government should reduce alleged commissions and inefficiencies if there is no corruption at present, and provide relief to the public.

title: Qatar Airways announces ‘limited’ flights to and from Doha
byline: Qatar Airways has announced a limited flight schedule to and from the Qatari capital, Doha, as the US-Israeli war on Iran roils air travel in the region.

title: EU leaders reject military involvement in Strait of Hormuz amid war on Iran
byline: European leaders have rejected demands by United States President Donald Trump ⁠to help ensure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz as foreign ministers from the European Union gathered in Brussels to discuss skyrocketing oil prices during the US-Israeli war on Iran.

title: Dubai airport resumes some flights after drone attack caused fuel tank blaze
byline: Dubai’s ​international airport was gradually resuming flights on Monday after a fuel tank fire caused by a drone attack forced ‌a temporary suspension, spotlighting the challenge for regional carriers grappling with the Middle East crisis.
